items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: I’ve played and met the Queen Mother twice

ctx.x: And people have asked me “if you wanted to re-live two weeks of your life, or a week in music, which week will you choose?” And I think it would be those two weeks with him. I used to sit on the stage, Monk — they’d do “The Lady is a Tramp” to finish, you know,

he and Ella with the Basie band. You’re Ella, I mean you’re Basie, and facing the other way, and I’m this close to you. And there’s reams of music, reams of music, and Basie’s looking going clink, you know. Frank goes “I get too hungry” and Basie goes bonk bonk, bonk bonk. All this music. So finally one night Frank sang “I get too hungry/for dinner at eight.” And Basie goes [scats] and Sinatra turns around and said, “Bill, be careful, you might get a hernia.” But oh, he was so great. And out of all the people…
